name: Ebb (GRAIL-A)
intro: Ebb was one of two twin spacecraft, each about the size of a washing machine, that chased each other around the Moon to map its gravity. When their fuel ran low in December 2012, NASA steered both into a mountain near the north pole. Ebb hit first.
whyLeft: Its orbit was sinking and its fuel was almost gone, so NASA chose a safe, remote mountain to crash it into rather than risk hitting a historic site.
repurpose: The crash site is now a memorial named for astronaut Sally Ride, and its small crater is a fresh test of how the Moon heals scars.
funFact: Fourth graders from Emily Dickinson Elementary School in Bozeman, Montana, won a contest to name the twins Ebb and Flow.

hotspots.title: Ebb’s crater
hotspots.text: Ebb hit the southern face of a mountain about 2.5 km tall, near a crater called Goldschmidt. LRO later found its new crater, only a few metres wide.

source.label: NASA JPL: GRAIL impact site named for Sally Ride

photo.alt: An orbital view of a slope with a small dark-rimmed new crater
photo.caption: Ebb’s impact crater, photographed by NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter after the crash.
photo.licenseEvidence: LROC images (NASA/GSFC/Arizona State University) are free for educational use with credit; this site is an educational NASA Space Apps project.

hotspots.title: MoonKAM
hotspots.text: Ebb carried a camera that students could aim. Three days before the crash it filmed the Moon’s surface sliding past below. This is real footage from that camera.

source.label: NASA JPL: GRAIL impact site named for Sally Ride

video.caption: Real MoonKAM video from Ebb, recorded on 14 December 2012, three days before impact.
video.licenseEvidence: NASA SVS page 11186 (“All of our content is in the public domain unless otherwise noted”); Commons copy marked “Public domain”; sound removed

hotspots.title: Last engine burn
hotspots.text: Fifty minutes before impact, both twins fired their engines until the tanks ran dry. Measuring exactly how much fuel was left helps engineers plan future missions.

source.label: NASA JPL: GRAIL impact site named for Sally Ride

hotspots.title: Looking home
hotspots.text: Earlier in the mission, Ebb’s MoonKAM photographed Earth far beyond the Moon’s far side. Student teams chose many of the targets.

photo.alt: The lunar far side with Earth in the distance, photographed by Ebb
photo.caption: Earth beyond the Moon’s far side, photographed by Ebb’s MoonKAM in March 2012.

hotspots.title: Gravity map
hotspots.text: By measuring tiny changes in the distance between them, Ebb and Flow made the most detailed gravity map of any world at that time, revealing hidden lumps under the Moon’s surface.

source.label: NASA: GRAIL impact sites, craters about 5 m with dark ejecta (depth estimated)
